subject: Learning Methods
title: Dual Coding Theory
description: A fast breakdown of Dual Coding Theory for builders.

hook.text: Allan Paivio discovered that words paired with images are remembered twice as well as words alone.

buildup.text: Your brain has separate channels for verbal and visual information. Each creates its own memory trace.

discovery.text: When you encode something both verbally and visually, you get two independent retrieval routes.

twist.text: This is why doodling while listening can help recall. The sketch creates a second code alongside the words.

climax.text: Draw a diagram. Sketch a timeline. Visualize the concept. Give your brain two ways to find it later.

punchline.text: Words plus pictures. Two codes beat one.

quiz.question: Why are words paired with images remembered better?
options: Images are more interesting than text
Two separate memory codes create two retrieval routes
The brain processes images faster than text
